taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes American ranid genus arrangements are contested (Lithobates vs Rana); the batch name follows NatureServe's Lithobates. NatureServe does not recognize subspecies.
fieldMarks: Green, brownish or bronze (nearly black when cold) with dark spots
A straight ridge along each side of the back from behind the eye that does not reach the groin
Hind legs crossbanded; toe webbing does not reach the tip of the 5th toe
Male eardrum much larger than the eye, throat may be yellow; up to 10.8 cm
behavior: Call is a single croak or series, like a plucked loose banjo string
Males call mainly May-August in the north
Often leaps into water with a 'squeenk' when approached
Inactive in cold weather; many overwinter in small streams
habitat: Almost any permanent or semi-permanent water and vernal pools.
range: Eastern United States and adjacent southeastern Canada. Introduced in Newfoundland, British Columbia, Washington and Utah.
